risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement: Randomisation and allocation concealment were properly performed. And no differences were found between the analysed groups.

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement: Participants, carers, and those delivering the interventions were probably aware of the assigned groups, as blinding was not feasible. Although potentially deviations from the intended interventions were identified (the number of embryos transferred was lower in blastocyst group: 1.1 blastocyst vs 1.4 cleavage), it doesn´t seem to affect the outcome as blastocyst group still had better results. No other deviations or differences were reported that could plausibly have influenced the outcomes. The analysis was conducted according to the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle.
